intent: In-place backward walking cycle: the two legs alternate positions, the pelvis shifts laterally with the step rhythm, the upper body leans slightly backward, the neck and head maintain a backward-tilted posture, and the arms/shoulders change subtly with the leg rhythm.

phases.name: start-pose-to-passing-1
phases.description: From the offset-leg pose at the start of the loop to passing 1.

phases.name: passing-1-to-opposite-leg-pose
phases.description: Opens into the opposite-leg pose; the pelvis continues shifting along +X to its maximum.

phases.name: opposite-leg-pose-to-passing-2
phases.description: From the opposite-leg pose to passing 2.

phases.name: passing-2-to-loop-return
phases.description: Opens again and closes the loop back to the starting pose.

keyPoses.description: Loop start/end marker with the two legs in an offset pose.
Clear leg-retraction marker in the first half-cycle.
Mid-cycle marker where hips X reaches its maximum.
Clear leg-retraction marker in the second half-cycle.

weightTransfer.description: The pelvis shifts laterally along +X from f0 to its maximum at f23, then shifts back until f45; no specific support leg is assigned.
weightTransfer.contactCaveat: There is no contact/force track. The evidence shows the pelvis trajectory and changes in leg pose, but does not reliably confirm which leg bears weight at each frame.

bodyMechanics.description: The two half-cycles coordinate in this order: leg marker 1 at f8 → passing 1 at f12 → pelvis X maximum at f23 → leg marker 2 at f30 → passing 2 at f34. The upper body leans slightly backward; the neck and head maintain a backward-tilted posture throughout the cycle; the arms/shoulders change more subtly than the leg rhythm. The evidence is not sufficient to conclude gaze direction beyond the backward-tilted head posture.
coordinationFocus: leg marker 1 f8 → passing 1 f12 → pelvis X maximum f23 → leg marker 2 f30 → passing 2 f34
slight backward lean of the upper body
backward-tilted neck and head posture throughout the cycle
subtle arm and shoulder change relative to the leg rhythm

recommended: timing of leg-position changes with lateral pelvis shift
subtle upper-body and arm counter-motion in a backward walk
